name: Monster / Creature Horror
definition: A dangerous being violates assumed safety, and characters must learn enough about its behavior to survive while confronting what the creature reflects or disrupts.
negative_signals: uncertainty located entirely inside one character's perception
diagnostic_questions: Does the creature have consistent capacities and behavior?
Does fear grow through encounters that teach usable information?

neighbors.distinction: Creature horror gives the threat material agency beyond uncertain perception.
Creature horror promises survival from predation or violation rather than reciprocal understanding.

reader_promises.name: Creature rules
reader_promises.description: Establish capacities, limits, traces, and behavior through consequential encounters.

reader_promises.name: Escalating exposure
reader_promises.description: Move from signs to encounters to unavoidable confrontation without exhausting fear too early.

roles.name: Survivor
roles.description: Adapts behavior as evidence replaces comforting assumptions.

roles.name: Creature
roles.description: Pursues needs or patterns that remain coherent even when not humanly moral.

roles.name: Denier or exploiter
roles.description: Suppresses evidence, underestimates risk, or tries to use the creature.

conflicts: Destroying danger versus understanding its ecology
stakes: Preservation of a community or habitat
settings: Ordinary place with hidden access routes

movements.name: Trace
movements.description: Reveal an effect that implies an unknown dangerous agency.

movements.name: Partial encounter
movements.description: Show enough capability to invalidate the first safety plan.

movements.name: Rule learning
movements.description: Turn losses and observation into a usable but incomplete model.

movements.name: Confrontation or containment
movements.description: Apply accumulated knowledge under changed conditions and accept the cost.

complications.name: Incomplete model
complications.description: A learned rule is real but applies only to one stage, individual, or condition.

complications.name: Spread
complications.description: The threat has reproduced, migrated, or altered more territory than expected.

complications.name: Human exploitation
complications.description: A person protects or directs the creature for another objective.

twists.name: Not hunting
twists.description: Behavior interpreted as predation serves defense, reproduction, or containment of something worse.

twists.name: Survivor marked
twists.description: Prior contact changed a survivor's relationship to the creature.

conclusions.name: Contained
conclusions.description: Characters exploit established limits to stop immediate spread.

conclusions.name: Escape with threat
conclusions.description: Survival is earned while evidence shows containment remains incomplete.

conclusions.name: New boundary
conclusions.description: Understanding permits a costly coexistence or withdrawal.

subversions: Make the creature consistent while human institutions create the worst escalation.
Let containment require restoring an ecological boundary.
cliches_to_avoid: Rules that change solely to enable a jump scare
Characters ignoring established evidence without motivation
quality_checks: Each encounter reveals or tests a rule.
Fear includes anticipation and consequence, not only attacks.
The ending uses knowledge earned earlier.

sources.title: The Cambridge Companion to Science Fiction
sources.contribution: Notes horror's recognizable intrusion of unnatural danger and its potential combinations with science fiction.

sources.title: A Checklist for Critiquing Science Fiction
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: Supports consistent rules, environmental credibility, motivated reactions, and causal plotting.
